sentences.text: Olivier Le Peuch, a French national born in 1963 or 1964, has served as chief executive officer and a director of SLB since August 2019, leading the company's global strategy, operations and long-term vision and its transformation into a global technology company.

sentences.quote: He earned a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, and a master's degree in microelectronics, both from ENSEIRB-MATMECA and University of Bordeaux.[4]
sentences.text: He holds an electrical engineering degree and a master's in microelectronics from ENSEIRB-MATMECA and the University of Bordeaux, and joined Schlumberger in 1987 as an electrical engineer.

sentences.quote: Prior to becoming CEO, he served as chief operating officer. He has also held several key executive positions, including executive vice president of Reservoir and Infrastructure; president of the Cameron Group; president of Completions; vice president of Engineering, Manufacturing, and Sustaining; and president of Schlumberger Information Solutions.
sentences.text: Before becoming CEO he was chief operating officer, and earlier held roles including executive vice president of Reservoir and Infrastructure, president of the Cameron Group, president of Completions, and president of Schlumberger Information Solutions.

sentences.quote: In 2023, Le Peuch's total compensation from Schlumberger was $17.2 million, representing a CEO-to-median worker pay ratio of 154-to-1.
sentences.text: His reported total compensation was about 17.3 million dollars.

sentences.text: SLB's Data Center Solutions business is scaling fast, with revenue up 63% year on year in the first half of 2026 and management targeting a run rate above $1 billion annualized by end-2026 and more than $2 billion as it exits 2027.

The Kelvion acquisition adds cooling technology to SLB's engineering, modular manufacturing and digital capabilities, with the combined data center businesses expected to generate over $2 billion of pro forma 2026 revenue.
Digital annualized recurring revenue exceeded $1 billion at the end of the first quarter of 2026, up 15% year on year.
Management guided fourth-quarter revenue above $10 billion, roughly 5% higher year on year, at about a 24% adjusted EBITDA margin.
